# @zakkster/lite-crdt

> Operational CRDTs for @zakkster/lite-store. A last-write-wins map (LWW-Map) and an observed-remove set (OR-Set) whose converged state is projected into a reactive lite-store. Op-based, transport-agnostic, order-independent and duplicate-tolerant, with full-state sync for late joiners and an optional zero-config cross-tab transport. Single-file ESM, zero runtime dependencies.

Version: 2.0.0 [2.0.0] adds `doc.list(name)` -- an RGA positional sequence with `insert(index, value)`, `values()`, `ids()`, `size` and a read-only `.store` projection. Order is deterministic and replica-independent (concurrent same-origin inserts descend by `(lamport, replicaId)`); an insert whose origin anchor is unseen is buffered and integrated when the origin arrives, never dropped. [2.0.0] adds list DELETE: `delete(index)` and `deleteById(bl, br)` emit an `ldel`, which sets a MONOTONE per-element `del` flag (once deleted, never resurrected) and splices the value out of the projection; the birth ANCHOR stays linked, so a concurrent insert that named the deleted element as its origin still lands. An `ldel` delivered BEFORE its birth `lins` records a placeholder tombstone (keyed by the birth anchor, capped at the same 4096 pending budget, fail-closed on overflow) so the element is born-dead on every replica. `delete(index)` fails closed (`misconfigured`) on an out-of-range/non-integer index; `deleteById` on a missing or already-deleted element is a no-op returning `false` (consistent with OR-Set `deleteById`). [2.0.0] adds list MOVE: `move(fromIndex, toIndex)` emits an `lmv`. MOVE is a first-class LWW POSITION REGISTER `(ml, mr) -> anchor` whose value is drawn from the anchor space -- NOT delete+reinsert, NOT a live-element reference. Applying an `lmv` UNCONDITIONALLY mints + integrates a fresh anchor (id == the move's `(l, r)`) at the destination origin (so a concurrent insert naming this move's anchor as its origin still lands, win or lose), then CONDITIONALLY writes the register under `tsWins(l, r, ml, mr)`: only a move beating the element's current register stamp relinks the element to the newly minted anchor. A losing (lower-stamped) move leaves its minted anchor ABANDONED (occupying no element), so two concurrent moves of one element converge to ONE position on every replica. Move and delete COMMUTE (disjoint fields: monotone `del` flag vs LWW register) -- a deleted element stays invisible under any move and is never resurrected. An `lmv` before its birth `lins` records a born-moved placeholder (shared pending budget); an `lmv` whose destination origin is unseen pends on the shared origin buffer. `toIndex` semantics: the destination index AFTER the element is removed -- `move(from, to)` == `arr.splice(to, 0, arr.splice(from, 1)[0])`; a self-move `move(i, i)` is a no-op that still converges. `move` fails closed (`misconfigured`) on an out-of-range/non-integer index; the classic RGA backward-typing interleaving is inherent, not a bug (pinned by test). `list` op types are `lins`/`ldel`/`lmv`. NOTE: this is a forward-only 2.0 break -- a 1.x peer throws `malformed_op` on `lins/ldel/lmv` and cannot consume list frames. [2.0.0] adds list STATE SYNC: `getState()`/`mergeState()` round-trip the sequence -- each anchor node stores its ORIGIN so `mergeState` re-runs RGA integration from origins in ASCENDING `(l, r)` (never trusting a transmitted sibling order; an orphan node whose origin never arrives is dropped + reported), and elements merge by the same `tsWins` register / monotone-delete algebra as the live ops (idempotent + commutative with a replayed op log). `getStateSince(V)` ships a node when `node.l > V[r]` and an element when any of its three OWN-writer stamps (birth `(bl,br)`, move register `(ml,mr)`, remover `(dl,dr)`) beats `V` -- per-writer filtering is sound because the record stores each mutation's own writer (the OR-Set `removed` full-ship hazard does not recur). `compact(V)` gains list compaction (two tiers; see below). State shape: `{ kind:"list", nodes:{ "r#l":[or,ol] }, elems:{ "br#bl":[ml,mr,anchorKey,del,dl,dr,v] } }`, keys sorted, split on `lastIndexOf("#")`.

## Mental model

- lite-crdt is the authoritative mutation API; lite-store is a reactive read-model (projection). You mutate through CRDT methods (which emit ops) and bind your UI to `collection.store`. You cannot derive correct ops from a transparent proxy's writes, hence this inversion.
- `collection.store` is a READ-ONLY lite-store proxy. Writing to it throws `CRDTError("readonly")`. Mutate via `.set()/.add()/.delete()` only.
- [1.1] The guard is DEEP: nested objects/arrays reached through `.store`, `get()`, `values()` or
  `entries()` are wrapped too, so `map.store.cfg.theme = x` throws instead of mutating state with
  no op emitted. Nested views are WeakMap-cached, so identity is stable across reads.
- [1.1] Map `keys()/values()/entries()/snapshot()` are SORTED by key, not insertion-ordered:
  replicas learn keys in different orders, so insertion order is not replica-independent.
- [1.1] `"__proto__"` is not a usable map key: local `set()/delete()` throw
  `CRDTError("misconfigured")`; an incoming remote op with that key is ignored (a peer must not
  be able to crash a replica with one crafted op).
- [1.2] A `"__proto__"` COLLECTION name or OR-Set element id is fine, unlike a map key: `getState()`
  builds its output over `Object.create(null)`, so such a name/id becomes an own key that
  round-trips through `getState -> mergeState` intact (no prototype is retargeted, no throw added).
- [1.1] `counter.inc(by)/dec(by)` require an integer within Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and throw
  `CRDTError("misconfigured")` otherwise; non-positive `by` remains a documented no-op.
- Every op is commutative AND idempotent by construction. No seen-set is required; transports may reorder and redeliver freely.

## Installation

```
npm install @zakkster/lite-crdt
```

Peer dependencies: `@zakkster/lite-store` (^1.0.0) and `@zakkster/lite-signal` (^1.1.3). Zero runtime dependencies of its own. ESM only. `node >= 18`.

## Exports

- `createCRDTDoc(options?)` -> doc
- `connectBroadcastChannel(doc, channelName)` -> `{ dispose() }`  (optional cross-tab transport over native BroadcastChannel)
- `CRDTError` (class; `.code` is one of `kind_mismatch | malformed_op | readonly | misconfigured`)

## createCRDTDoc(options)

options: `{ replicaId?: string, clock?: number, onError?: (e) => void, undoDepth?: number }`. A caller-supplied `replicaId` MUST be globally unique per logical replica: the whole `(lamport, replicaId)` total order and every OR-Set tag (`replicaId + "#" + n`) assume it, and two replicas sharing an id diverge silently [1.2.1]. A PROVIDED `replicaId` is now validated to a non-empty string and `createCRDTDoc` throws `misconfigured` otherwise (a non-string or empty id would emit ops every peer's door drops -> a silent one-way divergence); only an omitted id is auto-generated [1.3.1]. If omitted it is auto-generated from crypto (122-bit `crypto.randomUUID`, or a 128-bit `getRandomValues` fallback -> a 34-char `"r-..."` id). The crypto source is resolved once at module load: the Web Crypto global (browsers, Node >= 19) or the `node:crypto` builtin (Node 18.x, whose default runtime lacks the unflagged global) -- a Node builtin, not a runtime dep. Only in a realm with NEITHER (no Web Crypto global and no node:crypto) does `createCRDTDoc` FAIL CLOSED with a `misconfigured` error rather than mint a weak id; that is a genuine last resort, not the common case -- supply an explicit `replicaId` there [1.2.1]. `clock` is assumed monotonic per replica: the Lamport clock only advances, so do not reset it downward. `onError` receives errors thrown by `op`/`change` listeners (which are otherwise isolated) AND every remote op/state the validation door drops (a malformed field, a kind-mismatch, a malformed merge payload) [1.1.2]. `undoDepth` bounds the local undo/redo rings (default 100; 0 disables history).

doc surface:
- `doc.replicaId: string`
- `doc.clock(): number` -- current Lamport time
- `doc.map(name): LWWMap` -- get/create an LWW-Map (cached by name; throws `kind_mismatch` if the name exists as an array)
- `doc.array(name, opts?): ORSet` -- get/create an OR-Set; `opts.identify?: (value) => string | number` (defaults to `(v) => v.id`)
- `doc.counter(name): PNCounter` -- get/create a PN-Counter (cached by name; throws `kind_mismatch` if the name exists as another kind) [1.1]
- `doc.list(name): RGAList` -- get/create an RGA positional sequence (cached by name; throws `kind_mismatch` if the name exists as another kind) [2.0]
- `doc.transact(fn): T` -- run fn; buffer its ops and flush as ONE `ops` frame + one coalesced `change`; reactive readers update once (runs in a lite-signal batch); nested transacts flush at the outermost close; ops before a throw still flush; returns fn's value [1.1]
- `doc.undo(): boolean` / `doc.redo(): boolean` -- invert the last local edit / re-apply it; each is itself a local edit that EMITS an op, so peers converge; returns false if the ring is empty [1.1]. Undo of an OR-Set removal restores MEMBERSHIP and VALUE, not list position: the re-add mints a fresh tag, so the element reappears at a re-timed index, never necessarily its old one (contract: decisions/0003) [1.2.1]
- `doc.canUndo(): boolean` / `doc.canRedo(): boolean` / `doc.clearHistory(): void` [1.1]
- `doc.applyOp(op): void` -- apply a remote op; idempotent and commutative; NEVER re-emits; auto-creates the collection if unseen, inferring kind from op type. STRICT: a non-op envelope or an unknown op type throws `malformed_op`; a malformed field or a kind-mismatch is DROPPED and reported to `onError` (reject-and-continue), never applied [1.1.2]
- `doc.applyOps(ops): void` -- apply a batch. RESILIENT: never throws on one bad frame -- a strict throw or a dropped op is routed to `onError` and the batch continues, so every good frame still applies. The transport-safe path a custom transport uses [1.1.2]
- `doc.getState(): DocState` -- serialize full converged state (JSON) for hydrating a late joiner; collection names are emitted SORTED, so two converged replicas produce byte-identical output [1.2]
- `doc.mergeState(state): void` -- merge a remote full state (idempotent, commutative); a malformed collection/register is dropped and reported to `onError`, never crashes [1.1.2]
- `doc.versionVector(): { [replicaId]: lamport }` -- a prototype-free, JSON-serializable snapshot of the doc's per-writer version vector (max Lamport observed from each writer). Hand it to a peer for a delta request [1.3]
- `doc.compact(V): number` -- PURELY LOCAL memory reclamation: drop every causally-stable tombstone (LWW delete, OR removed-tag, and the OR value register of a stable NON-member) that every replica in the frontier `V` has already observed. Emits nothing, adds no op type, changes no wire byte; returns the count reclaimed. Safety is the CONSERVATIVE global frontier `minAck = min(V.values())` -- drop a tombstone with lamport `l` iff `l <= minAck`. TWO ASSUMPTIONS, or compaction diverges: (a) `V` MUST be the pointwise-min version vector EVERY replica has acknowledged (collect each replica's `versionVector()` and take the per-key min) -- a frontier ahead of a lagging replica drops a tombstone that replica's concurrent op still needs to lose to and RESURRECTS it; (b) your transport MUST NOT redeliver ops older than the compaction frontier -- compaction narrows the package's "reorder and redeliver freely" guarantee, because once a below-frontier tombstone is dropped, a redelivered pre-frontier `add` resurrects a dead element. A delta-based transport (`getStateSince`) or one that stops replaying acknowledged ops satisfies (b) for free. A malformed `V` is reported to `onError` and reclaims nothing (fail closed, never throws). `getState()` may legitimately shrink after compaction; the observable `snapshot()` never changes [1.3]. [2.0.0] `compact(V)` also reclaims `list` state in TWO tiers. Tier 1 (always, at `minAck = min(V.values())`): a deleted element whose delete AND move-register stamps are both causally stable (`del && dl <= minAck && ml <= minAck`) has its payload `v` + record dropped, KEEPING the bare anchor node (it may still be named as an insertion origin). Tier 2 (anchor UNLINK) requires GLOBAL QUIESCENCE and is the one new caller contract: only when `minAck >= max(V.values()) && minAck >= doc.clock()` -- every replica at the SAME frontier AND this doc's clock no further ahead, so no op naming any anchor can still be in flight -- may a truly unoccupied anchor (hosting no live element and no live element's birth home) be unlinked from the chain. This is the ONLY sound discharge of "no future op names this anchor" from a version vector, alongside decisions/0004's no-redelivery-below-frontier assumption. If a single replica lags (so `minAck < max(V)`) or the local clock is ahead of the frontier, Tier 2 does NOT unlink -- unlinking then would let that replica's concurrent op resurrect the anchor. A compacted anchor never resurrects: replaying the full op log after compaction leaves the converged sequence unchanged
- `doc.getStateSince(V): DocState` -- the `getState()` shape filtered to just what a peer at version vector `V` has not yet seen (per-writer `l > V[r]`; counters ship FULL, being small and max-idempotent). A valid PARTIAL state consumed by the SAME `mergeState` door, so `peerAtV.mergeState(sender.getStateSince(peerAtV.versionVector()))` converges the peer in one delta frame instead of a full dump. Empty `V` yields the full state; a malformed `V` fails closed to a full `getState()` [1.3]
- `doc.on('op', cb): () => void` -- locally-generated ops, one call per op; forward these to your transport; returns a disposer
- `doc.on('ops', cb): () => void` -- batched local ops: one call per `transact` (or a 1-op array per single edit); the built-in BroadcastChannel transport uses this so a transaction is one frame [1.1]
- `doc.on('change', cb): () => void` -- any convergent state change (local or remote); returns a disposer
- `doc.snapshot(): object` -- plain deep copy of every collection; top-level collection names are key-sorted and each collection sorts its own keys, so the snapshot is replica-independent (converged replicas stringify byte-identically) [1.2]
- `doc.dispose(): void` -- release signals and clear listeners; subsequent mutations and applyOp are silent

## LWWMap (doc.map)

Keyed register map; last write wins under a `(lamport, replicaId)` total order; deletes are timestamped tombstones competing with writes.

- reactive reads: `get(key)`, `has(key)` (fine-grained: re-run only when that key changes); `keys()`, `values()`, `entries()`, `size` (coarse: re-run on any change)
- mutations (emit ops): `set(key, value)`, `delete(key)`
- `store` -- read-only reactive lite-store projection (object); writing throws
- `snapshot()` -- plain object of present entries
- keys are coerced to strings.

Resolution: set-vs-set and set-vs-delete both resolve by higher lamport, tie broken by higher replicaId string. Re-delivery is a no-op.

## ORSet (doc.array)

Observed-remove set keyed by a stable element id, with a last-write-wins value register per id.

- reactive reads: `has(value)`, `hasId(id)`, `get(id)`, `values()`, `ids()`, `size` (coarse)
- mutations (emit ops): `add(value)` / `push(value)` (alias), `delete(value)`, `deleteById(id)`
- `store` -- read-only reactive lite-store projection (array); writing or calling a mutator (push/splice/...) throws
- `snapshot()` -- plain array in order

Semantics:
- A fresh `add` mints a unique membership tag. Concurrent add vs remove is ADD-WINS.
- Re-adding a present id edits its value (last-write-wins) WITHOUT a new tag and WITHOUT changing order. This is the key DX choice vs a textbook OR-Set: edits do not reorder the list.
- `delete`/`deleteById` removes only the tags the caller has observed; a concurrent add of a new tag survives.
- Order is deterministic across replicas: by each element's first-add `(lamport, replicaId)`.
- Elements must have a stable id (via `identify` or an `id` field); a missing id throws `misconfigured`.

## PNCounter (doc.counter) [1.1]

Positive-Negative counter: two grow-only per-replica maps (increments P, decrements N); value = sum(P) - sum(N).

- reactive read: `value()` (subscribe); untracked `peek()`; `size` getter aliases `value()`
- mutations (emit ops): `inc(by=1)`, `dec(by=1)` -- non-positive `by` is ignored
- `snapshot()` -- plain number
- Convergence: ops carry the replica's NEW cumulative P (or N); apply takes MAX per replica. Idempotent (re-max is a no-op) and commutative (max is). NO lamport -- counters converge by max, not total order. Use for votes/likes/reactions/presence.

## RGAList (doc.list) [2.0]

RGA (Replicated Growable Array) positional sequence: an ordered list with first-class insert, delete and MOVE. Element identity is an immutable BIRTH anchor `(l, r)`; position is fixed at integration by the RGA scan (concurrent same-origin inserts descend by `(lamport, replicaId)`), so order is deterministic and replica-independent. See decisions/0006.

- reactive reads: `size` (live element count), `values()` (visible order; nested objects come back read-only), `ids()` (per-element birth-anchor id `"r#l"`, stable across moves), read-only `.store` array projection (writing throws `readonly`)
- mutations (emit ops): `insert(index, value)` -> birth id `"r#l"` (emits `lins`); `delete(index)` (emits `ldel`, returns true); `deleteById(bl, br)` (emits `ldel` iff live, else no-op returning false); `move(fromIndex, toIndex)` (emits `lmv`, returns true)
- `insert`/`delete`/`move` fail closed (`misconfigured`) on an out-of-range/non-integer index; `move` `toIndex` is the destination AFTER removal (`move(from,to)` == `arr.splice(to,0,arr.splice(from,1)[0])`); `move(i,i)` is a converging no-op
- `snapshot()` -- plain array of the visible sequence
- Model: delete = a monotone `del` flag (never resurrected); MOVE = a first-class LWW position register `(ml,mr) -> anchor` whose value is a freshly minted anchor id (NOT delete+reinsert, NOT a live-element reference) -- so move||delete COMMUTE and concurrent moves of one element converge to ONE winner. An out-of-order `lins`/`lmv` (unseen origin) or `ldel`/`lmv` (unseen birth) PENDS (capped 4096, fail-closed on overflow), never drops. The classic RGA backward-typing interleaving is inherent, not a bug (pinned by test).
- Full state-based sync: `getState`/`mergeState` (re-integrates from origins in ascending `(l,r)`, never trusting a transmitted order; orphan dropped+reported), `getStateSince(V)` per-writer delta (sound: the record stores each mutation's own writer), and two-tier `compact(V)` (see doc.compact). The 2.0 break is forward-only: a 1.x peer throws `malformed_op` on `lins/ldel/lmv` and drops `kind:"list"` state; core-three wire format unchanged.

## Operation wire format (JSON)

- LWW set: `{ t:"set", c, k, v, l, r }`
- LWW delete: `{ t:"del", c, k, l, r }`
- OR add: `{ t:"add", c, id, n, v, l, r }`   (tag = `r + "#" + n`)
- OR update (value only): `{ t:"upd", c, id, v, l, r }`
- OR remove: `{ t:"rm", c, id, g:[tagKey...], l, r }`
- Counter inc: `{ t:"cinc", c, r, p }`   (p = replica's new cumulative increments; NO `l`)
- Counter dec: `{ t:"cdec", c, r, n }`   (n = replica's new cumulative decrements; NO `l`)
- List insert: `{ t:"lins", c, l, r, or, ol, v }`   (`(l,r)` = birth anchor id; `(or,ol)` = origin, `or:null` = HEAD) [2.0]
- List delete: `{ t:"ldel", c, l, r, bl, br }`   (`(bl,br)` = target birth anchor; `(l,r)` = remover stamp) [2.0]
- List move: `{ t:"lmv", c, l, r, bl, br, or, ol }`   (`(bl,br)` = target birth; `(l,r)` = register stamp + minted anchor id; `(or,ol)` = destination origin) [2.0]

`c` = collection name, `l` = lamport, `r` = replicaId. Ops are emitted only for local mutations. `push` of a present id emits `upd`; of an absent id emits `add`.

## Transports

- Manual: `doc.on('op', op => send(op))` out; `doc.applyOp(received)` in. Works over WebSocket, WebRTC, server fan-out, or a watched JSON file.
- Cross-tab: `connectBroadcastChannel(doc, channelName)` subscribes to `ops` (so a transact() burst is ONE frame) and runs a request/state handshake to hydrate late joiners; receive side accepts both `ops` and legacy single-`op` frames. Uses native BroadcastChannel; no dependency. Returns `{ dispose() }`.

## Errors

`CRDTError` with `.code`:
- `kind_mismatch` -- a collection name already exists as the other kind
- `malformed_op` -- applyOp received a non-op or unknown op type
- `readonly` -- attempted to mutate a `.store` projection directly
- `misconfigured` -- bad listener registration, missing element id, or BroadcastChannel unavailable

## Constraints and non-goals (v1)

- Values are held by reference locally and copied over the wire; treat them as immutable (pass new objects to edit; do not mutate stored objects).
- No RGA / positional sequence / reorder / rich text. Order is causal, not index-positional.
- Tombstone GC is now opt-in via `doc.compact(V)` [1.3]: LWW tombstones, OR removed-tags and OR value registers for stable non-members are reclaimed once a supplied version-vector frontier proves them causally stable (every replica has observed them). Without calling `compact`, they accumulate O(distinct ids seen) as before; an OR-Set member's live-membership entry is still dropped the moment its last tag is removed, so live-membership retention is O(live ids), not O(ops) [1.2]. `compact` is purely local and changes no wire byte.
- Browser globals (BroadcastChannel) are only required by `connectBroadcastChannel`; the core is environment-neutral.

## Minimal example

```js
import { createCRDTDoc, connectBroadcastChannel } from "@zakkster/lite-crdt";
import { effect } from "@zakkster/lite-signal";

const doc = createCRDTDoc({ replicaId: crypto.randomUUID() });
const todos = doc.array("todos");
const conn = connectBroadcastChannel(doc, "todo-room");   // cross-tab

effect(() => renderList(todos.values()));   // reactive UI

todos.push({ id: "1", text: "buy milk", done: false });
todos.push({ id: "1", text: "buy milk", done: true });    // edit, no reorder
todos.deleteById("1");
```
